name: An Albuquerque courtyard

place_source.title: Wikidata: Albuquerque (Q34804), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A walled courtyard in Albuquerque's North Valley: cottonwood and mesquite shade a patch of bare earth, a bird bath draws doves and finches, and roadrunners stalk the walls while bats hunt moths at dusk.

facts.text: Albuquerque has a cold semi-arid climate (Köppen BSk), with hot summers, cool winters, and about 235 mm of rain a year, much of it in the summer monsoon.

source.title: Wikipedia: Albuquerque, New Mexico
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Albuquerque, New Mexico", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The Rio Grande bosque, a cottonwood-willow riparian forest, runs through Albuquerque along the river and provides habitat for roadrunners, hawks, and dozens of bird species.

source.title: Wikipedia: Rio Grande bosque
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Rio Grande bosque", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The greater roadrunner is New Mexico's state bird, common in Albuquerque's yards and open spaces, where it hunts lizards, snakes, and insects on foot.

source.title: City of Albuquerque: Common Wildlife
source.attribution: City of Albuquerque, Common Wildlife page, CC BY-SA 4.0
